analysis:
The only change in this file is at line 313, in the test helper that records server stream events. The patch adds `.logprobs` to the `case .toolCall, .toolCallDelta:` arm, which continues past those events. Units 3 and 4 are unchanged base text from lines 654 to 1810 of the same test file. I treated them as surrounding context only.

The change touches test code only, with no production source. It does not alter the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract, key custody, App Attest authorization, the encrypted prefix cache (T-041), TB-007 engine behavior, or any trust boundary. The new arm only makes the switch over `MLXServerGenerationEvent` exhaustive for a new `.logprobs` case. In these tests it silently drops logprobs events from the recorded output.

I saw no loosening of a security control. The surrounding tests cover KV reslice grants, tool-choice enforcement and think-tag handling. They assert fail-closed behavior and are unaffected.

One question remains for later passes. The production change that introduces the `.logprobs` event, including any code that serializes or encrypts logprobs in `inference_chunk` responses, is outside the supplied evidence. A reviewer should confirm that the new event is encrypted and fail-closed (T-008) and does not leak plaintext. I found no basis for a finding in this file.
